subject: Human Body
title: The Leg and Knee
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Leg and Knee usable.

hook.text: The femur is the longest, heaviest bone in your body. It can withstand forces of 1,700 pounds.

buildup.text: Below the knee, two bones share the load: the tibia bears weight while the fibula stabilizes the ankle.

discovery.text: The kneecap floats inside the quadriceps tendon. It acts as a pulley, boosting leg extension by 30%.

twist.text: The knee lacks bony stability. It depends entirely on ligaments and muscles. That's why knee injuries are so common.

climax.text: Your knee absorbs 3 to 5 times your body weight with each step. Running multiplies that force even more.

punchline.text: The knee does the hardest job with the least protection.

quiz.question: How does the kneecap help with movement?
options: It acts as a pulley to boost leg extension
It connects the femur to the tibia
